newsitem.title: ROMANIA: ROMANIA INTERBANK LEU, RETAIL RATES LOWER.
newsitem.headline: ROMANIA INTERBANK LEU, RETAIL RATES LOWER.

text.p: Romania's leu currency drifted lower to 6,050/6,080 to the dollar against 5,965/995 in early trading on an interbank market affected by hard currency shortages.
Operators said intrabank trading saw larger volumes on Tuesday and predicted the leu would continue to edge down against the greenback in the coming days.
"I see the leu drifting marginally down in the next few days," said a trader with one of the four dealer banks.
"The market seems more liquid over the past days as foreign investors showed up on the capital market," another said.
Romania's capital market saw higher volumes and prices over the past month, with foreigners starting to take an interest in Romanian equities.
Latest central bank data showed interbank volume was $9,000 on Monday, when overall trading stood at $9.05 million.
Leu-dollar retail rates weakened to 6,200/500 after they lingered at about 6,100/200 over the past two weeks.
Traders said they expected Romania's new centrist coalition government to announce its reform package this week after ending talks with international lenders.
One-week fund rates hovered at 75-75 percent on a money market short of leu funds. -- Mirela Eremia, Bucharest Newsroom 40-1 3120264
